title: UNEMPLOYMENT (GLASGOW AND BIRMINGHAM).
text: MACLEAN asked the Minister of Labour whether he can state for a convenient date in the month of October, 1930, 1931, 1932, 1933, and 1934, the total number of registered unemployed for the Labour Exchange areas of Birmingham and Glasgow, showing, respectively, the number in receipt of standard benefit, the § Date.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT (DURHAM).
text: STOREY asked the Minister of Labour the number of insured workers in the general engineering, marine engineering, and building industries registered as unemployed at the Sunderland, Pallion, and Southwick-on-Wear Employment Exchanges at the latest convenient date; and what percentage these figures represent of the insured workers in these industries registered at those exchanges? § Lieut.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT AND DISTRESSED AREAS.
text: Since September, 1931, the total number of unemployed persons on the registers of the employment exchanges in these areas has fallen by 65,000, and the fall since June, 1932, which was perhaps the worst period, amounts to over 100,000.

Gentlemen opposite deplore it—that the figure of registered unemployed should still be above the 2,000,000 mark, we rejoice, and I think others should rejoice, that it is the smallest figure recorded in any month for the last five years.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT ASSISTANCE ACT, 1934.
text: If we take the whole country, out of the 1,700,000 registered unemployed, 620,000 are applicants of the Board, and even if we add the additional number which will be taken over on the second appointed day, I think that we shall still find that more than half the registered unemployed are on standard benefit.
By way of contrast, may I draw an illustration from my own constituency? In Port Glasgow last December there were 3,200 registered unemployed, which represented about 40 per cent.
